TOPIC_REFERENCE: Real-Time Media Transport — WebRTC and Audio Perception
SECTION_TITLE: Production Grounding: Why Real-Time Media Drops Frames
SECTION_BODY:
A common beginner misconception is that real-time systems pick UDP simply because they do not care about quality and just throw away dropped packets. In production systems, real-time media engineering is vastly more nuanced and sophisticated.

The Human Biology Constraint: The 150 ms Rule

The International Telecommunication Union standard (ITU-T G.114) specifies that for natural, interactive two-way human conversation, one-way mouth-to-ear delay must remain below 150 milliseconds. When latency exceeds 200 ms, speakers begin unintentionally talking over one another, pausing awkwardly, and asking: "Sorry, go ahead—no, you go."

In live voice communication, late data is worthless data. Hearing what someone said 400 milliseconds ago is actively harmful if it delays the words they are speaking right now. This is why interactive media protocols build on raw UDP, adding sophisticated user-space controls:

Incoming audio packets traverse an adaptive Jitter Buffer💡 Jitter BufferAudio Playback QueueA dynamic, small user-space buffer (typically 20 ms to 40 ms) that temporarily holds received audio packets so they can be played back to the speaker at a smooth, constant cadence despite erratic arrival times across the internet.. If an audio packet is lost permanently, codecs like Opus apply Packet Loss Concealment (PLC)💡 Packet Loss Concealment (PLC)Acoustic SynthesisAn algorithm in modern audio decoders (like Opus) that mathematically synthesizes a plausible continuation waveform based on the pitch and harmonic timbre of preceding audio packets, masking short gaps without stalling playback.. To prevent losses before they happen, senders embed Forward Error Correction (FEC)💡 Forward Error Correction (FEC)Parity MathTransmitting mathematical parity bytes bundled alongside subsequent data packets, allowing the receiver to reconstruct a lost packet instantly without waiting for a retransmission round-trip..

The Architectural Mental Model

TCP buys correctness by letting time stretch. UDP buys time by making correctness the application's problem.

When absolute data integrity is non-negotiable—such as database transaction logs, financial balance sheets, and JSON API payloads—we choose TCP and accept latency jitter. When temporal freshness is non-negotiable—such as live voice, video conferencing, and multiplayer game movement—we choose UDP and handle loss in user space with jitter buffers, FEC, and loss concealment.
